title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: In one sentence, who decides which step comes next in a workflow, and who decides it in an agent?
In your makerspace assistant, the code always runs search_manuals on the student's question, then makes one model call that writes an answer from the top three pages. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: An agent, because it calls a search tool and uses a language model
An agent, because the model writes the final answer in its own words
A workflow, because the code fixes the steps and the order they run in
Neither, because a workflow cannot include any language model calls at all

items.stem: A system gives the model three tools (search_manuals, check_calendar, book_slot) and the goal "help this student". After each tool result, the model picks the next tool or writes its answer; the code only runs the chosen tool and stops after 10 steps. What is it?

options.text: A workflow, because the program runs the tools and sets a step limit
An agent, because the model chooses each next step from the results
A workflow, because the same three tools are offered on every request
Neither, because the program and not the model runs the chosen tools

items.stem: Which makerspace task is the strongest candidate for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Emailing each new member the same safety checklist after they sign up
Reformatting every booking confirmation into one standard calendar entry
Looking up a machine's opening hours and replying with them each time
Diagnosing a "my print failed" report where each check depends on the last

items.stem: A teammate says, "Agents are more capable, so the whole assistant should be an agent." Your sponsor's model budget is small. Which reply is best?

options.text: Flexibility costs extra model calls and predictability, so use an agent only where steps can't be fixed in advance
Agreed, since an agent can do whatever a workflow does and costs about the same per request
Agreed, as long as the agent uses a larger model, because a larger model removes the cost problem
Disagree, because a workflow is always cheaper and better however varied the student requests are

items.stem: Booking a machine always goes: check the calendar, confirm the slot with the student, then write the booking. In one or two sentences, give a reason this part should be a fixed workflow rather than an agent.
